calls.head: The Hurricanes should pile up the shots
calls.body: The Hurricanes shoot a lot, and the Canucks are one of the league’s worst at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.
calls.call: The Hurricanes take at least their usual 66.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Carolina 2nd for shot volume (66.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Vancouver 30th for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: Carolina took 59.4 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 66.6.

calls.head: The Canucks can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Hurricanes’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Canucks’ kill is one of the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Canucks more than most.
calls.call: The Hurricanes’ power play creates at least their usual 8.0 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Carolina 8th for power play (8.0 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 28th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: Carolina’s power play created 21.5 expected goals per 60 in 3:10 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.0, and scored 3 goals.
calls.beyond: Carolina’s power play created 21.5 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.0 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 175 games.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 83% chance, and Carolina delivered.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 17% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Carolina got the good looks
surprises.body: Carolina’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

surprises.head: Vancouver tried a different line
surprises.body: E. Pettersson, J. DeBrusk, J. Lekkerimäki played 12:14 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Vancouver’s usual lines.

story.head: Stankoven’s hat trick, one at every strength
paras: The Hurricanes had this one put away early. K'Andre Miller opened the scoring 1:18 in. Andrei Svechnikov added two power-play goals. It was 3-0 before the first period was half over. Logan Stankoven scored three: one shorthanded, one on the power play and one at even strength. Vancouver pulled Kevin Lankinen after six goals.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Hurricanes win nine in ten. By our Swing measure, Shayne Gostisbehere had the best night of anyone. The Canucks tried a line they hadn’t used before: Elias Pettersson, Jake DeBrusk and Jonathan Lekkerimäki, and it had a hand in both of their goals.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Hurricanes.
Elias Pettersson has a point in every game this season.
K'Andre Miller scored his first goal of the season.
Whether the Canucks keep that line together in New Jersey on Saturday.
